headline: 28 trades net -2.1 bps/bet (-60 bps total); last-9 window +6.3 bps net — still far too thin to judge.
regime_note: BTC ~$78.1k, holding the upper $76-81k band where recent short-side fades have mostly resolved favorably; the loss-heavy cluster sits earlier near $63-66k. Signal is flat (0), so nothing is live right now.
assessment_md:
**How it's doing.** Over the full live ledger of 28 resolved trades, the strategy is running slightly negative: -2.1 bps per bet on average, or about -60 bps cumulatively, with a 35.7% win rate. The most recent 9-trade window looks better (+6.3 bps net, 44% wins), but that swing is dominated by a handful of large winners (e.g. +48.7 and +25.9 bps) offset by big losers (-28.1, -13.2 bps). This is exactly the kind of high-variance, small-sample picture where the average is unstable.

**What changed vs last time.** Essentially nothing material — still 28 trades, same ~-2.1 bps mean and -60 bps total. The rolling window ticked from ~+10 to +6.3 bps. No new resolved trades of consequence; recent signals (Sep 15, Sep 17) were small losers around -4 bps.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us.** They do confirm the strategy is marginal by design: gross edge ~4 bps against a ~3.9 bps breakeven cost leaves little room. They do NOT tell us the edge is broken — 28 trades is nowhere near enough to distinguish a dead signal from normal noise, and the negative total is well within what variance can produce. Separately, the edge-search still finds 0 survivors at a 5 bps cost bar on both venues.

**Bottom line.** Behaving roughly as expected for a marginal, likely-not-net-profitable signal. No degradation alert warranted, but no evidence of durable profit either. Keep collecting data before concluding anything.
